title: The Crazy idea for the roof
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：crazy　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 crazy 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1993 the operator wrote of ① a crazy idea for the roof in the log, and everybody in the station said at once that it was ② crazier than the one named there the year before. Three shifts on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the operator, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the crazy ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the craziest idea for the roof anybody in the station had ever seen, or so the log for June 1987 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too crazy to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the trainee who had come to help; the crazy ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the switch at the far screen, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a crazy love of the sea, and said that no trainee in his right mind would call it ⑥ as crazy as the love of the sea they had once had in the old station. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was crazy or not, and he said so.

By 2000 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the log. What the line asked for was ⑦ something crazy, and nothing besides. The trainee from the next station called the whole plan ⑧ quite crazy; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the log kept the names of the crazy ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 2003, in silence, she wrote of another crazy idea for the roof in the same log, and the work, which took two shifts, seemed ⑨ crazier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The craziest love of the sea in the whole station, she said in 2005, was the one she could never quite name; the crazy ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 疯狂（前置定语 a crazy idea for the roof：1993 年操作员在运行日志里记下的那件疯狂的构想）
B. adj. 疯狂／着迷（比较级 crazier than：文中两处，一处比屋顶的构想，一处比预想）
C. adj. 疯狂／着迷（最高级 the craziest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 疯狂（表语 too crazy to do：母亲觉得它太疯狂，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 着迷（前置定语 a crazy love of the sea：叔叔把整件事称作一桩着迷的痴迷）
F. adj. 着迷（同级比较 as crazy as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩对海的痴迷相比）
G. adj. 着迷（后置定语 something crazy：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 着迷（受程度副词修饰 quite crazy：那位实习生的评价）

items.q: a crazy idea for the roof
the craziest idea for the roof anybody
a crazy love of the sea
The craziest love of the sea in

answers.why: crazy 意为“疯狂”，1993 年操作员在运行日志里记下的是“一件疯狂的构想”，此处作前置定语 a crazy idea for the roof。
crazy 意为“疯狂”，此处用比较级 crazier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
crazy 意为“疯狂”，运行日志上 六月 那行字说它是机房里最疯狂的一件，故用最高级 the craziest idea for the roof。
crazy 意为“疯狂”，母亲认为这件东西“太疯狂了，谁也用不上”，too crazy to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
crazy 意为“着迷”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩着迷的痴迷”，此处作前置定语 a crazy love of the sea。
crazy 意为“着迷”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩对海的痴迷一样着迷”，同级比较用 as crazy as。
crazy 意为“着迷”，运行日志上那半行字要的是“着迷的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something crazy。
crazy 意为“着迷”，邻机房来的那位实习生认为这套计划“相当着迷”，quite 修饰原级 crazy。
crazy 意为“着迷”，2003 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要着迷”，故用比较级 crazier than。
crazy 意为“着迷”，母亲 2005 年说的是“整个机房里最着迷的那一桩”，故用最高级 the craziest love of the sea。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1993 年，操作员在运行日志里记下了一件疯狂的构想。（a crazy idea for the roof）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更疯狂。（crazier than …）
母亲觉得它太疯狂，谁也用不上。（too crazy to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩着迷的痴迷。（a crazy love of the sea）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩对海的痴迷一样着迷。（as crazy as …）
到了 2000 年，运行日志上只剩半行字：要的是一件着迷的东西。（something crazy）
answers: In 1993 the operator wrote of a crazy idea for the roof in the log.
Everybody said it was crazier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too crazy to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a crazy love of the sea.
He said nobody would call it as crazy as the love of the sea they had once had.
By 2000 the log asked for nothing but something crazy.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 crazy 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1993 the operator wrote of a crazy idea for the roof in the log, and nobody forgot it.
It was the craziest idea for the roof in the station, or so the log says.
My mother thought it too crazy to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a crazy love of the sea, and nobody argued with him.
The trainee from the next station called the plan quite crazy, and everybody laughed.
The crazy ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
